text.text:
Minimal Bone? Meet Tornier® HRS Max.
The next step in our shoulder innovation journey.

The Tornier HRS Max System is purpose-built to handle complex humeral reconstructions, expanding our comprehensive shoulder portfolio. The modular functionality of HRS Max is designed to allow surgeons to create constructs that address massive proximal bone loss, with the goal of rebuilding patient anatomy and providing freedom of movement.

Possibilities. Built piece by piece.
 HRS Max expands your reconstructive power. Intuitive trialing streamlines each step, so you can focus on precision, efficiency, and patient outcomes.

text.text:
A. Perform compatibility

HRS Max features Perform polyethylene insert compatibility – giving you a cohesive platform to adapt to your patient’s need.

text_copy.text:
B. Data driven design

HRS Max leverages Stryker’s SOMA (Stryker Orthopedic Modeling and Analytics) database, a comprehensive collection of shoulder anatomy data derived from thousands of CT scans. SOMA’s deep anatomical insights shaped the system’s deltoid wrapping bodies, providing designs that align with the realities of massive proximal bone loss.

text_copy_319419805.text:
C. Tapered connections

HRS Max uses Morse tapers, allowing for streamlined implant assembly during complex reconstructions.

text_copy_2066554464.text:
D. Suture holes

HRS Max features suture holes every 90 degrees for soft tissue attachment needs.

text_copy_1643481011.text:
E. Multiple fixation modes

HRS Max allows for press-fit or cemented applications in cases of massive proximal humeral bone loss.

text.text: Join surgeons who choose Tornier HRS Max and strive to restore stability, function, and hope in complex humeral reconstructions.
Tornier HRS Max is a prosthesis used during shoulder arthroplasty to treat cases of massive proximal humeral bone loss.
HRS Max can be used in anatomic, reverse, and hemi shoulder arthroplasty. For the full list of indications, warnings and cautions please refer to the IFU.
HRS Max can be press-fitted or cemented, allowing a surgeon versatility in complex cases of massive proximal humeral bone loss.
